### How does the player install addons in WoW TBC Anniversary?

Addons are small UI tools that the player installs in the AddOns folder, then enables on the character screen. After login, the addon menu or slash command opens settings and the UI changes right away. ### How can the player keep the UI readable after adding addons?

The player can keep the screen readable by hiding extra icons, and placing frames near the edges. Leatrix Plus helps drop small chores, and BlizzMove helps place windows in a calm spot. ### What does Attune do during attunement chains?

Attune shows the full attunement chain and marks progress in one window. The player types /attune, checks the next step, and can also view guild progress when friends use the same addon. ### How do Questie and Leatrix Maps help during leveling?

Questie marks quests on the map and shows objectives, so the player follows a route with clear targets.

WoW Classic Mists of Pandaria Classic Discussion

[Ghur-656206](https://us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/u/Ghur-656206) (Ghur) February 25, 2021, 3:24am 1

Hi all,  
I’m working on an addon to help with the long attunement chains present everywhere in TBC.

The addon gives you a visual representation of where you are in the attunement chain, what the next steps are and what you’ll need.  
It also allows you to ‘survey’ your guild (and groups/raids) to know where they are at and know who is on the same attunement step as you.

In this guide, I want to highlight Attune, an excellent addon that enables you to track guild and personal attunement progress.

## **What is Attunement?**

If you are new to WoW Classic or the Burning Crusade, you may be wondering what attunement is. In short, attunement is a series of quests and objectives you need to complete to enter a dungeon or raid. If you want to raid, you need to be attuned. These quests can range from minor tasks to obtaining dropped items from other instances.

In TBC, these attunement questlines can become overwhelming if you don’t have a good way to track them.

This is where Attune comes in.

## **How does the Attune addon work?**

Attune keeps track of your character’s progress in completing the requirements to enter each one of the many BC dungeons and raids.

It does this by providing an easy-to-digest tree that shows the steps required to complete attunement. You can also hover over the steps to get more information about the quest or requirements.
For example, one of the first attunements players will work on in Burning Crusade is for the Black Morass dungeon. To begin this process, you need to hit level 66 and then travel to the Caverns of Time. You then speak to the Steward of Time to accept a quest called [To The Master’s Lair](https://tbc.wowhead.com/quest=10279/to-the-masters-lair) . If I hover over the tooltip for that quest, I see that it is a solo quest that requires me to speak to another NPC.

Screenshot of Attune, a WoW Burning Crusade addon. Attune shows a tree map of all quests and objectives required for attunement to an instance.

In this case, speaking to another NPC is pretty straightforward. If the objective was more difficult, you would see that a party was required and maybe even get a set of coordinates to set a waypoint.

In addition to personal attunement tracking, you can also use Attune to survey your guild and track their progress as well.
This is a vital tool for guild and raid leaders to help members complete tasks so they don’t show up on raid night, unable to get into the raid.

After sending out a survey to a raid or guild group, Attune will provide a neat table showing group member progress for each attunement. For this to work, the group members must also have the addon installed as well. To give you an idea of what this looks like, the addon authors posted a screenshot to [CurseForge](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/attune) for their guild Divine Heresy.

Screenshot of guild report in Attune addon for WoW Burning Crusade Classic Source: Addon author from their [CurseForge](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/attune) page.

Now that you have a little taste for what Attune is capable of, let’s look at how you can use it.

## **How to install Attune**

You can install Attune by downloading it from CurseForge and manually placing it in your BC Classic addon folder.

### _**Attunement Surveys and Raid Planner**_

If you want to see how progress is going in your party, raid, or guild, you can click on the ‘Survey’ button. This will give you the option of which group you want to send the survey out to. From there, you can click on ‘Results’ to see where each member is in the process.

You can also see where each of your characters is in the process if you are trying to complete attunement on alts.
From the ‘Results’ tab, you can also access the ‘Raid Planner’ tool (or with **_/attune raid_** ). This allows you to create and store raid teams ahead of raid night. You can see which role each player falls into and whether they are attuned to that raid or not.

Once you have filled your raid spots, you can invite the group with one click.

For this feature to be helpful, each raider will need to have Attune installed and set up their role profile.

To set up raid profiles, you can follow these steps:

* **Open the Attune addon with _/attune_**
* **Click on ‘Results’**
* **Select ‘Show Profiles’**
* **Set your Status and Role**

### TBC Anniversary Attunement Add-on

[TBC Anniversary Top Add-Ons](http://overgear.com/guides/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/tbc-anniversary-attunement-addons.png)

For TBC Anniversary, attunements are the quest chains or requirements that, once completed, let you enter certain raids or unlock key progression content, but tracking them manually can be tedious. That’s where the [Attune](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/attune) addon comes in: it gives you a clear visual of your attunement progress, showing each step of the required quest lines and letting you see who else in your group or guild is on the same step.

To use the addon after installation (either manually or via an addon manager), just type /attune in your chat box to open the interface. From here, you’ll see a tree or list of all attunement tasks, with completed steps clearly marked and pending steps highlighted—this helps you plan what to do next.
You can also use the Survey feature to collect attunement status from your guildmates, which is especially useful when organizing raids or checking who’s ready for specific content. It even includes some extra tools like a raid planner that uses collected data to help organize groups based on attunement status, and you can customize character roles or statuses to improve coordination.

For best results, make sure guild members also have the addon installed so that survey and progress-sharing features work properly.  
Alternatively, if you don’t want to go through the hassle of doing this yourself, we can handle [TBC Attunements](https://overgear.com/games/wow-20th-anniversary/phase-1-attunements) for you instead!
